THROW-FORWARD: Baobab Bomb

By: Laura Byrne | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Controversy rages over a massive new industrial project in Limpopo.

Unique Selling Point:
Thousands of protected indigenous trees including centuries-old baobabs are being bulldozed to make way for a new special economic zone costing billions in Limpopo. But while government promises it will provide thousands of jobs and transform the provincial economy, communities, environmental activists and farmers are up in arms.

Script:


UPSOUND: LINDY WILSON: This entire secrecy and lack of information has created huge concerns about this project.
UPSOUND: MPHATELENI MAKAULULE: This economic zone, it want to destroy that, the order which God created.
UPSOUND: DEIDRE CARTER: We are going to be importing pollution and exporting our valuable resources.
UPSOUND: MAKOMA LEKALAKALA: We cannot, like, commit ourselves to protecting and at the same time destroy.
VOICEOVER: The baobab. A symbol of our history and heritage.
UPSOUND: MPHATELENI MAKAULULE: Trees in Venda are our home in English. The higher me. When we have trees, we are at home because everything about the Venda is about the tree.
UPSOUND: DR SARAH VENTER: It’s the ancestor of trees, but it also harbours ancestors.
VOICEOVER: And the first casualty of a development tearing this landscape – and the community – apart.
UPSOUND: MAKOMA LEKALAKALA: How do we destroy the last unique forests we have for the sake of carbon intensive activities?
VOICEOVER: On an upcoming episode of Carte Blanche...
UPSOUND: MASA KEKANA: Thobela!
VOICEOVER: A massive new industrial zone in Limpopo promises to create thousands of jobs and revive our steel industry.
UPSOUND: MASA KEKANA: Well, looks like it’s already started.
UPSOUND: MATODZI RATHUMBU: It warrants us as this generation to say that we will innovatively and sustainably build the economy.
VOICEOVER: But as scarce resources and priceless heritage are threatened…
UPSOUND: DEIFRE CARTER: There’s no water in the towns, farmers are restricted. And the EIA says there is not sufficient water for the project.
VOICEOVER: …and controversy rages…
UPSOUND: LINDY WILSON: This project has already cost a billion rand – on what? There is nothing, literally nothing to show for a billion rand.
VOICEOVER: …we ask: What is the true cost of this multi-billion rand project?
UPSOUND: DEIDRE CARTER: I can say to you if the politicians were serious about the people of Limpopo, and thinking about the future, they would not be considering this project.
